text:
Edmonton arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, fresh off a 4-0 win at the Islanders in which Tristan Jarry (projected to start again) stopped all 18 shots. The Oilers are 3-1-1 in their last five, but they're without Zach Hyman (neck) and Isaac Howard. Colton Dach has taken Hyman's spot beside Kasperi Kapanen and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, and Kapanen has moved onto the first power-play unit. The Rangers have had five days off since a 6-3 home loss to LAK, and they're winless in three, outscored 18-11. Igor Shesterkin is on injured reserve.

Our numbers see an even game, with 2.98 expected goals for EDM and 3.07 for NYR, the quality of chances each side should produce. At five on five the two are close, 49% for EDM and 52% for NYR. Edmonton's results run ahead of its chances, a +17 goal difference on +5.1 expected. The Rangers take four penalties a game, and Edmonton's power play generates 0.91 expected goals a game against their 0.54 allowed on the penalty kill. In net, Jarry is at -1.9 goals saved above expected this season (-4.2 last year), while Dylan Garand, the projected Rangers starter, is at -0.2 (+3.9 in three games last season).

Connor McDavid brings a 14-game assist streak. As Jon Lane of NHL.com posted, it's "an NHL record season-opening assist streak." We give him a 91% chance at a point and 40% to score. Leon Draisaitl is at 43% to score. For New York, Alexis Lafrenière (15 points in 10 games) and Pavel Dorofeyev are each at 32% to score.
